Home/Car Detailing/Leather & Upholstery Detailing
Leather & Upholstery Detailing · West London

Leather & upholstery detailing

A deep clean and condition for leather seats, trim and upholstery — lifting grime, oils and stains, restoring suppleness and protecting against cracking and fading. Eco-friendly, pH-balanced, and fully mobile.

From £95 · free tailored quote
Call 07495 400369
Interior Specialists

Restore the feel of your cabin

Leather dries, cracks and discolours over time. Our pH-balanced clean lifts embedded dirt and dye transfer, then a premium conditioner restores softness and a protective finish guards against future wear.

  • Eco-friendly, pH-balanced leather-safe products
  • Dye-transfer, ink & stubborn stain removal
  • Premium conditioning to restore suppleness
  • Protective finish against cracking & fading
  • Fabric upholstery shampoo & extraction on request
What's Included

Cleaned, conditioned & protected

A careful, leather-safe process that leaves seats and trim looking, feeling and smelling refreshed.

Every Treatment Includes

  • Full vacuum of the interior to prepare surfaces
  • Gentle leather-safe cleaning using specialist solutions
  • Dirt and stain removal from seats, panels and trim
  • Leather conditioned with a premium balm to restore softness
  • Protective finish applied to guard against cracking and fading
  • Final detail check to ensure an even, natural look

Why Choose Ecoverde for Leather Care

  • We specialise in eco-friendly, safe detailing methods
  • Mobile service carried out at your home or workplace
  • Suitable for both modern and classic leather interiors
  • Restores comfort, feel and long-term durability
  • Trusted across West London for professional detailing
Fully Insured & DBS-Checked Eco-Friendly Products Fully Mobile — We Come to You 5.0 from 560+ Reviews
What Builds Up

What is actually on your seats

Leather in a car does not simply get dusty. It absorbs a specific mix of things, and each needs a different approach.

  • Body oils and perspiration. The main cause of the dark, slightly shiny patches on a driver bolster and the top of the backrest.
  • Denim dye transfer. Blue staining on cream, grey or tan seats, transferred from jeans. Very common and rarely shifted by ordinary cleaning.
  • Hand cream, sun cream and hair product. These leave a greasy film that traps dust and eventually turns grey.
  • Spilled food and drink. Sugar in particular goes sticky and then tacky in warm weather.
  • UV through the glass. Even in London, a car parked in daylight fades and dries the top surface of a dashboard and the tops of the seats.
Not All Leather

Different hides need different treatment

The single fastest way to ruin a car interior is treating every surface as though it were the same material. Before we clean anything we identify what we are working with.

TypeFound inHow we treat it
Pigmented or coatedMost modern carsHas a protective top coat. The most robust, and what standard leather cleaning is designed for.
Semi-anilinePremium and luxury cabinsLightly coated and more absorbent. Needs a gentler product and less moisture.
AnilineHigh-end and older classicsNo protective coating at all. It drinks in anything spilled on it, so cleaning is careful and minimal.
Nappa, often perforatedVentilated and heated seatsSoft and frequently punched with holes. Product must never be allowed to flood through the perforations.
Alcantara and suedeSports seats, trim, headliningNot leather at all. A leather balm will flatten and stain it. It is lifted with a dry foam and a soft brush instead.
Avoid These

Why household products damage car leather

Most of the badly damaged interiors we are called to were harmed by good intentions rather than neglect.

  • Baby wipes. The most common culprit. The surfactants and alcohol strip the protective top coat, which is what makes leather go dull and then crack.
  • All-purpose cleaner. Strongly alkaline. It will lift dirt and the finish with it.
  • Silicone dressings. They leave a high-shine greasy layer that attracts dust, feels unpleasant in summer and reflects badly in the windscreen.
  • Olive oil and other home remedies. Oil does not absorb into coated leather. It sits on top, goes rancid and attracts dirt.
  • Steam held too close. Heat and moisture together will lift stitching and shrink panels.

We use pH-balanced products worked in with a soft brush and lifted off with microfibre, then condition to replace what cleaning removes.

Keeping It

How often, and what to do between visits

For most cars a professional clean and condition every three to six months keeps leather supple and stops the top coat wearing through. If you park on-street, cover high mileage, or carry a dog or children, the shorter end of that is more realistic.

  • Wipe spills straight away. Almost every permanent stain we see was left overnight.
  • Keep a dry microfibre in the door bin rather than a packet of wipes.
  • Use a sunshade if the car sits in daylight all day.
  • Get in and out rather than sliding across the bolster, which is where wear always starts.
FAQs

Frequently asked questions

How do you clean and protect car leather seats?
We use eco-friendly, pH-balanced products that safely remove dirt, oils and stains, then apply a premium conditioner to restore suppleness and protect against cracking or fading.
Can you remove deep stains or dye transfer from leather?
Yes — we use specialist products and gentle techniques to lift dye transfer, ink marks and stubborn stains without damaging the finish. Each job is assessed first so we choose the safest, most effective treatment.
How often should I get my car leather detailed?
For most vehicles we recommend professional leather detailing every 3–6 months to preserve appearance, prevent wear and maintain a luxurious feel.
Do you offer mobile leather detailing across London?
Yes — we come to your home or workplace fully equipped with eco-friendly products and professional tools, across West and Central London.
How often should leather car seats be cleaned and conditioned?
Every three to six months suits most cars. Cleaning removes some of the oils that keep leather flexible, so conditioning afterwards is not optional. If the car lives on-street, covers high mileage or carries children or a dog, the shorter interval is more realistic.
Can you remove denim dye transfer from light-coloured leather?
Usually, yes. Blue transfer from jeans onto cream, grey or tan leather is one of the most common jobs we are asked about. It responds to a dedicated dye-transfer treatment worked gently rather than to ordinary cleaner. Very old transfer that has been left for years may lighten considerably rather than disappear entirely, and we will tell you which we expect before starting.
Can you clean perforated, heated or ventilated seats?
Yes, and they need a different technique. Product must never be allowed to flood through the perforations, because what goes through sits in the foam underneath and in the ventilation ducts. We work with a barely damp applicator and lift the product straight back off rather than saturating the surface.
Do you clean Alcantara and suede as well as leather?
Yes, but as a separate process. Alcantara is a synthetic microfibre, not leather, and a leather balm will flatten the pile and leave it patchy. It is cleaned with a dry foam and a soft brush, then the pile is lifted back up as it dries.
Are baby wipes safe to use on car leather?
No, and they are the most common cause of the damage we are called to fix. The surfactants and alcohol gradually strip the protective coating on the leather. It looks fine for a while, then goes dull, then cracks along the seams and bolsters, at which point cleaning cannot bring it back.
Can you repair leather that is already cracked or split?
Detailing cleans, feeds and protects leather, but it cannot rebuild a surface that has already broken. Cracking means the top coat has gone and the hide underneath has dried. That is a leather repair and re-colouring job. We will be straightforward about which of the two your seats need once we have seen them.
How long does leather detailing take?
A full interior leather clean and condition usually takes two to three hours depending on the size of the cabin and the condition it is in. Heavy dye transfer or ingrained soiling takes longer, because the work is done in stages rather than by scrubbing harder.
Will the seats feel greasy or look shiny afterwards?
No. A correctly conditioned seat should look like leather rather than like plastic, with a soft satin finish and no slip when you sit on it. The high-gloss look comes from silicone dressings, which we do not use.

Home/Car Restoration/Dent Removal & Panel Repair
Dent Removal & Panel Repair · West London

Dent removal & panel repair

Restore smooth, even bodywork — removing dents, dings and creases without disturbing your paint wherever possible. Ideal for car-park knocks, trolley dents and minor door damage, carried out at your home or workplace.

Quote on request · free photo assessment
Call 07495 400369
Paintless Where Possible

Smooth panels, original paint

Many small dents can be worked out without any filler or repainting — keeping your factory finish intact. Where paint is damaged, we'll advise the neatest, best-value route before any work begins.

  • Paintless dent removal for suitable dents
  • Trolley dents, door dings & minor creases
  • No filler or repaint where PDR is possible
  • Honest assessment from a few quick photos
  • Carried out at your home or workplace
Simple, Mobile, Honest

How mobile dent repair works

No body-shop visit and no courtesy-car hassle — just a quick, tidy repair at your door.

01

Send Us Photos

Message a few photos of the damage on WhatsApp with your postcode. We'll assess whether a paintless repair is possible and send a clear, upfront quote.

02

We Come to You

Our technician arrives at your West London address at the agreed time with everything needed — no need to visit a body shop.

03

Careful Repair

Using specialist PDR tools we gently work the dent back to its original shape, preserving your factory paint wherever possible.

04

Inspect & Drive Away

We walk you through the finished panel. In most cases dents are removed completely or dramatically improved.

Fully Insured & DBS-Checked Eco-Friendly Products Fully Mobile — We Come to You 5.0 from 560+ Reviews
How It Works

What paintless dent removal actually is

Paintless dent removal works the metal back to its original shape from behind, using specialist rods and picks, without filler and without repainting. Done properly the panel keeps its factory paint, which matters more than most people realise: original paint is worth money at resale and is the one thing a repair can never truly recreate.

  • No filler, no primer, no colour match to worry about.
  • The factory finish and its corrosion protection stay intact.
  • A car with original paint on every panel reads better to a buyer, an inspector or a lease returns agent.
  • It is usually quicker and cheaper than a conventional repair on the same dent.
Three Conditions

When PDR works, and when it does not

Paintless repair depends on three things being true at once. If any one of them fails, the honest answer is a different method.

  1. 1
    The paint must be intact

    PDR moves the metal, and the paint has to stretch with it. If the paint is already cracked, chipped or scratched through to primer, working the dent will only open it further.

  2. 2
    The metal must not be sharply stretched

    A soft, round dent has simply been pushed in and can be persuaded back. A sharp crease has stretched the metal past its limit, and stretched metal has nowhere to return to.

  3. 3
    There must be access behind the panel

    The tools work from the back. Double-skinned areas, bonded braces, structural adhesive and some door and roof sections leave no safe way in.

Dents right on the edge of a panel are the other common exclusion. The metal is doubled over and far stiffer there, so it resists reshaping.

Materials

Aluminium panels and modern high-strength steel

Bodywork has changed. Bonnets, wings and doors on newer cars are increasingly aluminium or high-strength steel, and both behave differently under a PDR tool.

MaterialFound onWhat it means for the repair
Mild steelMost older and mainstream carsThe most forgiving. Has a memory and wants to return to shape.
AluminiumBonnets, boot lids, many premium modelsMuch less springy, with little memory. Needs controlled heat, more time and considerably more skill.
High-strength steelModern safety structuresStiff and unforgiving. Some areas are not suitable for PDR at all.

We identify the panel material before quoting. An aluminium bonnet dent is a longer job than the same dent in a steel door, and it would be misleading to price them the same.

Realistic

Common dents, and what to expect

TypeTypical outcome
Door dings from the car parked next to youUsually removed completely. The classic PDR job.
Supermarket trolley dentsUsually removed completely where the paint is unbroken.
Hail damageOften excellent results across many small dents, and far cheaper than panel repairs.
Shallow creasesSubstantially improved, often close to invisible, occasionally not fully removed.
Sharp, deep creasesImproved rather than removed. We will say so before starting.

We would rather tell you a dent will be eighty per cent better than promise perfection and disappoint you. Where PDR is not the right answer we will say that too, and explain what is.

FAQs

Frequently asked questions

Can all dents be removed without repainting?
Not all — small dents without paint damage can often be removed paintlessly. We'll always advise the best option after seeing photos.
How long does dent removal take?
Most minor dent repairs take 1–3 hours, depending on the size and location of the damage.
Will the repair be visible afterwards?
Our goal is an invisible repair. In most cases dents are removed completely or significantly improved.
Do you repair creases and larger dents?
Sharper creases and larger dents may need paint or filler work — where that's the case we'll quote for a neat, colour-matched panel repair.
Can all dents be removed without repainting?
No, and anyone who says otherwise is overselling. Paintless repair needs three things at once: paint that is still intact, metal that has not been sharply stretched, and access to the back of the panel. Soft round dents with unbroken paint are ideal. Sharp creases, damage on a panel edge and dents in double-skinned sections usually need a different approach.
Will paintless dent removal damage my paint?
Not when the panel is suitable. The whole point of the method is that the factory paint stays on the car. The risk sits with dents where the paint is already compromised or the crease is sharp, because working those can open the paint further. That is exactly why we assess from photographs first rather than turning up and trying.
Can you repair a dent on an aluminium panel?
Often, yes, but it is a longer and more skilled job. Aluminium has far less memory than steel, so it does not want to spring back, and it usually needs controlled heat to become workable without cracking the paint. Many bonnets and boot lids on premium cars are aluminium, and we price those differently because they genuinely take longer.
Is paintless dent removal cheaper than a body shop?
Usually, and it is quicker. There is no filler, no primer, no colour matching and no curing time, and it is done at your address rather than leaving the car somewhere for days. It also preserves original paint, which is worth something in its own right when you come to sell.
Can you fix hail damage?
Yes, and it is one of the jobs PDR suits best. Hail typically leaves many small, shallow, round dents with the paint intact across bonnet, roof and boot, which is exactly the profile the method handles well. Repairing them conventionally would mean refinishing several panels at far greater cost.
Why can't you repair a dent on the edge of a panel?
The metal is folded over on itself at a panel edge, which makes it far stiffer than the middle of the panel and leaves very little room to work behind. It resists reshaping, and forcing it risks cracking the paint along the fold. Edge damage is usually better addressed with a conventional repair.
Will the dent be completely gone?
On a soft dent with sound paint and good access, usually yes. On a crease, or where the metal has been stretched, expect a substantial improvement rather than perfection. We will give you an honest expectation from the photographs, and we would far rather under-promise than talk you into a repair that cannot deliver what you were hoping for.
How long does a mobile dent repair take?
Most single dents take one to two hours at your home or workplace. Several dents, an aluminium panel or anything needing trim removed for access will take longer, and we will tell you the realistic time when we quote rather than on the day.

Home/Car Restoration/Bumper Scuff & Scratch Repair
Bumper Scuff & Scratch Repair · West London

Bumper scuff & scratch repair

Make scuffs and scratches disappear with a neat, colour-matched repair — carried out in place, without replacing the bumper. Perfect for kerbed bumpers, car-park scrapes and lease-return tidy-ups, done at your home or workplace.

Quote on request · free photo assessment
Call 07495 400369
Colour-Matched On Site

Scuffs gone, paint matched

Most scuffs and scratches are repaired and colour-matched exactly to your car, right where it's parked — no bumper replacement, no days off the road, no body-shop bill.

  • Colour-matched to your exact paint code
  • Repaired in place — no bumper replacement
  • Kerb scuffs, car-park scrapes & light scratches
  • Ideal before selling or handing back a lease
  • Fully insured, tidy, mobile service
Quick, Tidy, Mobile

How scuff & scratch repair works

A neat repair at your door, usually in a few hours — not days at a body shop.

01

Send Us Photos

Message photos of the scuff or scratch with your postcode. We'll confirm it's repairable in place and send a clear quote.

02

We Come to You

We arrive at your West London address with a mobile paint set-up and everything needed to colour-match your car.

03

Repair & Blend

We prep, fill and refinish the area, then colour-match and blend the paint for a seamless, factory-look finish.

04

Inspect & Drive Away

Once cured, we check the finish with you. The repair blends into the surrounding paint and your car looks its best again.

Fully Insured & DBS-Checked Eco-Friendly Products Fully Mobile — We Come to You 5.0 from 560+ Reviews
Plastic, Not Metal

Why a bumper is a different job to a wing

A bumper is not a panel. It is a moulded plastic cover that flexes, sits at the part of the car most likely to meet a kerb or a bollard, and behaves differently from the metal around it at every stage of a repair.

  • Plastic flexes, so the paint has to flex with it. A flexible additive goes into the primer and the paint. Standard panel paint sprayed onto a bumper will crack the first cold morning it is knocked.
  • Adhesion is the first problem, not the last. Bare polypropylene rejects paint unless it is properly cleaned and given an adhesion promoter. Most failed bumper repairs failed here.
  • Many bumpers have textured lower sections. These cannot be filled and flatted like a smooth surface. The texture has to be matched or the repair will stand out even in the right colour.
  • There is often a great deal behind it. Parking sensors, radar units, cameras and washer jets all live in modern bumpers, and none of them appreciate heat or filler dust.
Colour Match

Why your bumper may never have matched exactly

This surprises most people. If you look closely at your car in daylight, particularly a metallic, the bumper is often a very slightly different shade from the wing beside it. That is not damage and it is not a previous repair. It is how the car left the factory.

  • Metal panels are painted and then baked at a temperature that would deform plastic, so bumpers are painted separately, often in a different building.
  • Metal bodies are painted electrostatically. Plastic cannot hold that charge, so a different application method is used.
  • Metallic paint dries more slowly on plastic, which lets the metallic flake settle differently. The colour is the same; the way it reflects light is not.
  • A bumper also has far more curves than a wing, so the same paint reads differently as the light moves across it.

This matters for a repair. We match to the bumper as it actually is, not to the paint code alone, and we blend outward into the surrounding area so the eye never finds an edge.

In Place or Off

When a bumper can be repaired on the car

DamageRepaired in place?Why
Kerb and car-park scuffingYesThe most common job. Prepped, filled where needed, refinished and blended on the car.
Light scratches through the lacquerYesFlatted back and refinished locally.
Scuffing wrapped around a cornerUsuallyCorners are awkward but workable. We will confirm from photos.
Cracks and splitsSometimesA clean split can be plastic-welded from behind, which often means removing the bumper.
Tabs and mounts broken offNoIf the bumper no longer sits correctly on its mounts, refinishing it will not fix the gap. That is a replacement.

Send photographs straight on and from a low angle along the panel, which shows the depth of a scuff far better than a head-on shot.

Afterwards

Looking after a fresh bumper repair

  • Leave it two weeks before washing the repaired area, and wash by hand when you do.
  • No wax, sealant or ceramic for around a month. Fresh paint is still releasing solvent and needs to breathe.
  • No automatic car washes and no pressure washing close to the repair edge.
  • Park a little further from the kerb than you think you need to. Most bumpers we repair have been repaired before.
FAQs

Frequently asked questions

Can most bumper scuffs be repaired in place?
Yes — most scuffs and scratches are repaired and colour-matched on site, without replacing the bumper.
Will the repair match my paint?
We colour-match to your vehicle's exact paint code for a seamless, factory-look finish.
How long does a scuff repair take?
Most bumper scuff and scratch repairs take 2–4 hours, plus a little curing time, depending on the size of the area.
Is repairing cheaper than replacing the bumper?
Almost always — an in-place colour-matched repair is far cheaper than replacing and repainting a whole bumper, and keeps your original panel.
Can most bumper scuffs be repaired without replacing the bumper?
Yes. The great majority of kerb scuffs, car park scrapes and light scratches are repaired on the car and refinished in place. Replacement only becomes the sensible answer when the bumper is cracked through, or when the mounting tabs behind it have broken so it no longer sits square against the wing.
Why does my bumper look a slightly different shade to the rest of the car?
Because it usually left the factory that way. Metal panels are painted and baked at a temperature that would deform plastic, so bumpers are painted separately using a different method, and metallic flake settles differently on plastic as it dries. The paint code is identical, the way it reflects light is not. We match to your bumper as it is rather than to the code alone.
Will the repair crack when the bumper flexes?
Not if it is done correctly. A flexible additive goes into the primer and the paint so the finish moves with the plastic underneath. Repairs that crack in the first cold snap were done with standard panel paint and no flex additive, which is a shortcut we do not take.
Can you repair a textured or unpainted lower bumper section?
Often, yes, but it is a different technique. Textured plastic cannot simply be filled and flatted smooth, because a glass-flat patch in a grained surface is obvious from several feet away. The texture has to be recreated to match the surrounding area, and we will tell you honestly how close we expect to get.
What about parking sensors, cameras and radar behind the bumper?
We work around them carefully. Sensors, radar units for cruise control and reversing cameras all sit inside modern bumpers, and heat, dust and paint overspray can affect them. Where the damage sits directly over a sensor we will say so at the quote stage rather than discovering it halfway through.
How long does a bumper scuff repair take?
Most repairs are done in a few hours at your address, including curing time. Damage wrapped around a corner, or anything needing the bumper removed, takes longer, and we will tell you which yours is before you book rather than on the day.
Is it worth repairing scuffs before selling or handing back a lease?
Almost always. Lease companies charge for bumper damage at rates well above what a repair costs, and a private buyer reads a scuffed bumper as a sign the car has had a hard life. It is one of the highest-return jobs on a car about to change hands.
When can I wash the car after a bumper repair?
Leave it around two weeks, then hand wash gently. Avoid wax, sealant or ceramic coating for about a month, because fresh paint is still releasing solvent and sealing it too early traps that in. No automatic car washes at all in that period.

bodywork-paint-respraying-london.html:
Home/Car Restoration/Bodywork & Paint Respraying
Bodywork & Paint Respraying · West London

Bodywork & paint respraying

Professional, colour-matched respraying to restore damaged, scratched or faded panels to a factory-look finish. For deeper damage that's beyond polishing or paintless repair, a proper respray gives the longest-lasting, best-looking result.

Quote on request · free photo assessment
Call 07495 400369
Factory-Look Finish

Damaged panels, restored

When paint is chipped, deeply scratched or faded, respraying restores the panel far better than touch-up paint. We colour-match to your car and blend into surrounding panels for a seamless result.

  • Professional colour-matching to your paint code
  • Panel resprays for scratches, chips & fading
  • Seamless blend into surrounding panels
  • Longer-lasting than touch-up paint
  • Honest quote from photos before any work
Proper Paintwork, Done Right

How bodywork & respray works

A careful, colour-matched process that brings tired or damaged panels back to a factory-look finish.

01

Send Us Photos

Message photos of the damaged panels with your postcode. We'll assess the extent and send a clear, itemised quote.

02

Colour Match

We identify your exact paint code and mix a precise match, so the respray blends invisibly with your existing paintwork.

03

Prep & Respray

Panels are prepped, primed and resprayed to a professional standard, then blended into the surrounding areas.

04

Finish & Protect

Once cured, the finish is refined and, if you wish, protected with a sealant or ceramic coating to keep it looking new.

Fully Insured & DBS-Checked Eco-Friendly Products Fully Mobile — We Come to You 5.0 from 560+ Reviews
Finding The Colour

Your paint code is the starting point, not the answer

Every car carries a paint code, usually on a sticker in the door shut, under the bonnet or in the boot well. It tells us which formula the car left the factory with. What it does not tell us is what colour your car is today.

  • Paint fades. A car that has spent eight years parked outside in London is no longer the shade on the sticker, particularly in red, black and darker blues.
  • Manufacturers use variants. A single code often has several factory variants depending on plant and production year, and they are visibly different side by side.
  • Panels age at different rates. A roof and a bonnet take far more sun than a door, so they fade first.
  • Previous repairs change things. If a panel has been resprayed before, it may already be off the original code.

So we start from the code, then match to the actual panel in daylight, and adjust. Matching to the sticker alone is how you end up with a door that is technically the right colour and obviously wrong.

Paint Types

Solid, metallic and pearl are not equally easy

Paint typeHow it behavesMatching difficulty
SolidA single flat colour with no flakeMost straightforward, though solid reds and whites fade more than most
MetallicFine aluminium flake suspended in the colourHarder. The angle and speed of the spray change how the flake lies, and therefore the shade
Pearl and tri-coatA tinted mid-coat over a base, with a separate clearThe most demanding. Three layers must each be right, and the mid-coat thickness alters the colour
Matte and satinNo lacquer gloss at allSpecialist. It cannot be polished, so the finish must be right off the gun

If your car is a pearl white or a tri-coat, expect us to say so at the quote stage. They are entirely repairable, they simply take more time and more care.

Blending

Why we spray past the damage

A common question is why a repair to one corner of a wing involves paint going across most of the panel. The answer is that the human eye is extremely good at spotting a hard edge between two shades and very poor at spotting a gradual transition.

  1. 1
    Repair the damage itself

    Prepped, filled where necessary, primed and flatted until the surface is true.

  2. 2
    Lay the colour over the repair

    Built up in light coats rather than one heavy one.

  3. 3
    Fade the colour outward into the panel

    The new paint is thinned as it goes, so there is no line where old meets new.

  4. 4
    Lacquer the whole panel to a natural break

    A swage line, a shut or a body crease. Stopping mid-panel would leave a visible edge.

  5. 5
    Flat and polish the blend

    So the repaired area matches the texture and gloss of the paint around it, not just the colour.

Honest Limits

What suits a mobile repair, and what needs a booth

We are a mobile service and there is a real line here worth being straight about.

JobMobile?Notes
Localised scratches, chips and scuffsYesRepaired and blended at your address. This is what mobile refinishing is designed for.
A single panel with contained damageUsuallyWeather permitting. Paint needs dry, still, reasonably warm conditions.
Several panels, or a full resprayNoThat belongs in a spray booth with filtered air and controlled temperature. We will tell you rather than attempt it badly.
Rust that has gone through the metalNoPainting over corrosion hides it for a season and it returns. It needs cutting out and welding.
Structural or accident damageNoPanel alignment and safety structures come first, and that is bodyshop work.

Weather matters more than people expect. Damp, cold or windy conditions affect how paint lays down and cures, so we book refinishing work around the forecast rather than pressing on regardless.

Afterwards

Curing and looking after fresh paint

Paint is touch-dry within hours but is not fully hardened for weeks. What you do in that window decides how the repair looks in a year.

  • Leave it two weeks before washing, and hand wash gently when you do.
  • No wax, sealant or ceramic coating for about a month. Fresh paint is still releasing solvent and sealing it in too early causes it to cloud or soften.
  • No automatic car washes and no pressure washing near the blend edge.
  • Remove bird droppings and tree sap immediately. Fresh paint is far more vulnerable to etching than cured paint.
  • Avoid parking under trees or beside building work for the first few weeks if you can.

Once the paint has fully cured we are happy to come back and apply a sealant or a ceramic coating over it, which is the point at which protection actually helps rather than hinders.

FAQs

Frequently asked questions

Will the new paint match my existing colour?
Yes — we use professional colour-matching systems so the repaired area blends seamlessly with your original paintwork.
How long does paint respraying take?
Most panel resprays take 1–2 days, depending on the size and complexity of the repair and curing time.
Is respraying better than touch-up paint?
For visible damage, respraying gives a far superior and longer-lasting result than touch-up paint, especially on larger areas.
Will the new paint match my existing colour exactly?
That is the aim, and it is why we match to the panel rather than to the paint code alone. Your car has faded from the shade it left the factory in, and manufacturers often use several variants of the same code. We mix to the code, compare against the actual panel in daylight, adjust, then blend outward so there is no hard edge for the eye to find.
Where do I find my car's paint code?
Usually on a sticker in the driver's door shut, and otherwise under the bonnet, in the boot well or under the spare wheel cover. Send us a photo of it along with the damage and it saves a step. If you cannot find it we can identify it from the registration in most cases.
Why do you need to spray more than just the damaged area?
Because the eye finds a hard edge between two shades instantly and a gradual fade almost never. We repair the damage, then fade the new colour outward into the panel and lacquer to a natural break such as a swage line or a shut. Stopping at the edge of the repair is what makes a repair obvious.
Is a metallic or pearl finish harder to repair?
Yes. On metallic paint the aluminium flake lies differently depending on how it is sprayed, so two panels of identical paint can look different. Pearl and tri-coat finishes add a tinted mid-coat where the thickness itself changes the colour. Both are entirely repairable, they simply take more skill and more time, and we will flag it when quoting.
Can you do a full respray at my home?
No, and we would not claim to. Localised repairs and single-panel work can be done at your address in the right weather. A full respray belongs in a spray booth with filtered air and controlled temperature, because dust and airborne contamination land in wet paint. If that is what your car needs we will tell you honestly.
Can you paint over rust?
Not in any way that lasts. Surface oxidation can be treated, but where corrosion has gone through the metal, painting over it simply hides it for a season while it continues underneath. That needs cutting out and welding, which is bodyshop work, and we will say so rather than sell you a repair that will fail.
How long before I can wash the car or apply wax?
Wait around two weeks before washing, and hand wash gently. Leave wax, sealant and ceramic coating for about a month, because fresh paint is still releasing solvent and sealing it too early can cloud or soften the finish. Once it has cured properly we are happy to come back and protect it.
Does weather affect when you can respray?
Considerably. Paint needs dry, still and reasonably warm conditions to lay down and cure correctly, so damp, cold or windy days are a genuine problem for mobile refinishing. We book paintwork around the forecast, and we would rather move an appointment than deliver a finish that will not last.

Lease Return Valet · West London

Lease return valet

Handing your car back? A lease return valet is a thorough deep clean focused on exactly the areas leasing companies inspect — helping you avoid unexpected cleaning and condition charges. Fully mobile, and timed to your handover date.

Free tailored quote · book 1–3 days before handback
Call 07495 400369
Handback-Ready

Return your lease with confidence

Leasing companies charge for dirt, stains and neglect at inspection. We focus on the details they check most — inside and out — so your car presents at its best and you sidestep avoidable penalties.

  • Focused on the areas lease inspectors check
  • Full interior deep clean & odour freshen

Is This You?

This service is perfect if…

Lease return valets are all about avoiding charges and handing your car back looking its best.

  • You're worried about end-of-lease charges for dirt, scratches or stains
  • You have scuffs on alloys or light interior marks

  • You're unsure what condition your lease company expects
  • You want to avoid unnecessary penalties
  • You want a stress-free way to prepare your car for return
What's Included

What a lease return valet covers

A deep clean built around the leasing company's inspection checklist — inside, out and ready for handover.

Exterior

  • Full exterior safe wash — pre-rinse and paint-safe hand wash
  • Snow-foam pre-soak where suitable
  • Wheels cleaned — faces and barrels where accessible
  • Tyres dressed for a clean, factory-fresh look
  • Tar & bug removal on lower panels where needed
  • Light paint decontamination to remove bonded grime

  • Full interior deep clean — seats, carpets, mats & trims
  • Thorough vacuum including under seats and hard-to-reach areas
  • Dash, console & door cards cleaned to a careful, non-greasy finish
  • Interior windows cleaned for a clear finish
  • Light stain spot-treatment where possible
  • Odour freshen for a clean, neutral cabin

Handback Finishing

  • Finishing touches for handback day
  • Final walk-around check to ensure the car presents well
  • Photo-ready finish — ideal for inspection or handover

Optional Add-Ons

  • Paint correction for tired paintwork
  • Bumper scuff or alloy repair (quoted separately)
Fully Insured & DBS-Checked Eco-Friendly Products Fully Mobile — We Come to You 5.0 from 560+ Reviews
The Standard

What your lease company is actually measuring against

End of lease inspections in the UK are judged against the BVRLA Fair Wear and Tear standard, which almost every leasing and contract hire company signs up to. It draws a line between wear that comes from normal use, which you are not charged for, and damage caused by an event or by neglect, which you are.

  • Fair wear and tear is the gradual deterioration you would expect from ordinary use over the contract.
  • Damage is the result of an impact, careless loading, harsh treatment or something left undone.
  • The inspector works to a checklist, panel by panel, wheel by wheel. They are not forming a general impression of the car.
  • You are allowed to put things right beforehand, provided the work is done to a professional standard by a reputable repairer.

That last point is the one most people miss. Repairing before the inspection is nearly always cheaper than being charged for it afterwards.

The Charges

Where end of contract charges usually come from

AreaUsually acceptedUsually charged
Paint scratches and scuffsLight marks under roughly 25mm, about a thumb widthAnything longer, or through to primer or bare metal
Alloy wheelsLight scuffing on the rim edgeKerb damage to the wheel face, corrosion, buckling
InteriorNormal seat wear and light soilingBurns, tears, permanent staining, missing parts
SmellsA neutral cabinSmoke, pet and mould odours. Frequently the single largest charge, because it means deep cleaning or replacement
TyresEven wear, legal treadBelow the limit, uneven wear, damaged sidewalls, or a missing spare or repair kit
GlassSmall stone chips outside the swept areaCracks, or chips in the driver line of sight

A thorough valet addresses the interior, the smells and the general presentation. It will not remove a dent or a deep scratch, and we will tell you plainly which of your marks fall into which category.

Timing

When to book, and what to do on collection day

  1. 1
    Six to eight weeks before the return date

    Walk round the car in daylight and look at it the way an inspector will. Note every mark, then decide what is worth putting right.

  2. 2
    Sort any repairs first

    Kerbed alloys, bumper scuffs and dents are all cheaper to repair than to be charged for. Those are separate jobs from the valet and are best done before it.

  3. 3
    Book the valet close to the collection date

    A car valeted six weeks early will not look valeted on the day. A week or so ahead is about right.

  4. 4
    Photograph the car before it leaves you

    In daylight, all four corners, every wheel, the interior and the mileage. This is your evidence if a charge appears for damage you know was not there.

  5. 5
    Check you are handing back everything

    Both keys, the locking wheel nut, the parcel shelf, the charging cables, the handbook and the spare or repair kit. Missing items are charged at main dealer prices.

FAQs

Frequently asked questions

How does this valet help me save money on lease return?
We focus on the areas leasing companies check most, reducing the risk of cleaning and condition charges at inspection.
How long does it take?
Typically 3–4 hours, depending on the size and condition of the vehicle.
Can you fix scratches or dents before I return my car?
Light scratches and scuffs can often be improved on the day. Deeper damage may need bodywork or a scuff repair, which we can quote for separately.
When should I book before my handover?
We recommend booking 1–3 days before your return appointment, so the car is spotless for inspection.
What is the BVRLA fair wear and tear standard?
It is the industry standard almost every UK leasing company uses to judge a returned vehicle. It separates wear that results from normal use over the contract, which you are not charged for, from damage caused by an impact, careless treatment or neglect, which you are. The inspector works through a checklist rather than forming a general impression.
How big does a scratch have to be before I get charged?
As a general guide, light scratches and scuffs under about 25mm, roughly the width of a thumb, are usually accepted as fair wear and tear. Anything longer than that, or any mark that has gone through the paint to primer or bare metal, is likely to be charged. Standards vary slightly between companies, so check your own returns pack.
Will a valet stop me being charged at the end of my lease?
It removes one whole category of charge and helps with another. Interior condition and odours are assessed directly, and smoke, pet or damp smells are among the most expensive findings because they can mean deep cleaning or replacing trim. A valet will not remove a dent or a deep scratch, so if you have those, deal with them separately before the inspection.
Is it cheaper to repair damage myself before returning the car?
Nearly always, and you are entitled to. The standard allows you to have work done beforehand provided it is carried out to a professional standard by a reputable repairer. Lease companies charge for damage at rates that generally sit well above what the same repair costs privately.
When should I book the valet before my lease ends?
About a week before collection. Any earlier and the car will not look freshly valeted on the day, which is the only day that matters. If you also need repairs to wheels, bumpers or panels, book those first and the valet afterwards so the car is finished as a whole.
Do smoke or pet smells really matter?
They matter a great deal, and they are one of the most commonly charged items. A cabin that smells of smoke, animals or damp is treated as excess damage rather than wear, because putting it right can mean deep cleaning the entire interior or replacing trim and filters. It is worth addressing properly rather than covering with an air freshener, which an inspector will see through immediately.
Should I photograph the car before it is collected?
Yes, without exception. Take daylight photographs of all four corners, each wheel, the interior and the mileage on the day the car leaves you. If a charge appears afterwards for damage you know was not there, that record is the only thing that will settle it.
What else gets charged that people forget about?
Missing items, and they are billed at main dealer prices. The second key is the most common, followed by the locking wheel nut, the parcel shelf, charging cables on an electric or hybrid, the handbook and the spare wheel or tyre repair kit. Gather all of it before collection day rather than on it.

Ultimate Pre-Sale Valet · West London

Ultimate pre-sale valet

Selling your car? Reverse the signs of ageing and restore maximum value with a premium pre-sale package that goes far beyond a standard clean — machine polish, odour removal and ceramic-spray protection for a showroom-ready finish that helps your car sell faster, and for more.

From £289 · free tailored quote
Call 07495 400369
Showroom-Ready

Sell faster, for more

A well-presented car attracts more buyers and commands a higher price. This package restores shine, removes light scratches and odours, and protects the finish — so your listing photos and viewings make the best possible impression.

  • 1-stage machine polish to enhance gloss & remove light swirls
  • Micro-scratch removal to restore clarity
  • Deodorisation treatment for a fresh cabin
  • Spray-on ceramic coating for lasting protection
  • Engine bay cleaned for a professional presentation
Is This You?

This service is perfect if…

The Ultimate Pre-Sale Valet is built for anyone preparing a car for resale, trade-in or presentation to buyers.

  • You want to increase your car's resale value
  • You need your car looking showroom-ready for buyers
  • You're worried stains or odours could put buyers off
  • Your paintwork looks dull or tired
  • You want your car to stand out in listings and adverts
  • You want a quick, professional way to boost appeal
What's Included

Everything in the Ultimate Pre-Sale Valet

A premium, multi-stage detail that goes far beyond a standard clean — presentation and protection built to help your car sell.

Exterior

  • pH-neutral snow-foam pre-wash to safely loosen dirt and grime
  • Exterior hand dry & buff for a flawless, streak-free shine
  • Tyres dressed with a professional satin finish
  • Exterior trims conditioned to restore depth and protection
  • Wheel arches deep-cleaned to remove built-up debris

Interior

  • Full deep vacuum of interior, boot and hard-to-reach areas
  • Leather cleaning and conditioning for a supple, refreshed finish
  • Dashboard and interior plastics detailed and polished
  • Interior glass cleaned for a clear, streak-free finish

Premium Detailing

  • 1-stage machine paint correction to remove light swirls and enhance gloss
  • Micro-scratch removal to restore clarity and shine
  • Engine bay deep-cleaned for a professional presentation
  • Vehicle deodorisation treatment to remove unwanted odours
  • Spray-on ceramic coating for superior, long-lasting protection
Fully Insured & DBS-Checked Eco-Friendly Products Fully Mobile — We Come to You 5.0 from 560+ Reviews
Where You Sell

Three routes, judged three different ways

How much presentation is worth depends entirely on who you are selling to, and it is worth knowing before you decide how much to spend.

RouteHow the car is judgedWhat presentation is worth
Private saleBy a person who will fall for the car or walk away in the first minuteThe most. Buyers pay more for a car that feels cared for, and they haggle less
Online buying servicesAgainst a fixed condition checklist at inspectionReal but capped. A clean car passes inspection without deductions being found
Part exchangeBy a trade buyer valuing it against auction pricesThe least, though a filthy car still invites a lower opening offer

If you are selling privately, a full pre-sale valet is one of the highest-return things you can do to a car. If you are part-exchanging, a good clean is usually enough.

The Listing

Your photographs are the product

Nobody views a car they scrolled past. On a private sale the photographs decide whether the car is seen at all, and they are taken once, so they should be taken after the valet rather than before.

  • Photograph in soft daylight, early or late. Midday sun blows out the highlights and hides the paint.
  • Find a plain background. A quiet street or an empty car park. Wheelie bins and other cars make a listing look careless.
  • Shoot low and from the corners. Chest height flattens a car; kneeling makes it look like the brochure.
  • Photograph the wheels and the interior properly. These are the two things buyers zoom into.
  • Include the boot, the engine bay and the service book. Showing them signals you have nothing to hide.
First Minute

What a buyer notices before they look at anything else

Buyers form a view within about a minute of arriving, and it is rarely based on what the advert said. In order, this is what registers.

  1. 1
    The smell, before they have even sat down

    A stale, smoky or damp cabin is the single hardest thing to argue past, because it suggests neglect that goes beyond cleaning.

  2. 2
    The wheels and tyres

    Kerbed alloys read as careless ownership, fairly or not, and they are the first thing many buyers check.

  3. 3
    The glass, inside and out

    A smeared windscreen is noticed immediately from the driver seat and costs nothing to put right.

  4. 4
    The touch points

    Steering wheel, gear selector, door handles and seat bolsters. Shiny, greasy plastics suggest high mileage regardless of what the odometer says.

  5. 5
    The engine bay and the boot

    Few people expect these to be spotless, which is precisely why a tidy one makes an impression.

Worth It

The return, and being honest about it

A pre-sale valet is not cosmetic surgery. It presents the car you have at its genuine best so a buyer sees a cared-for example rather than a project, and so you have less to negotiate away.

  • A clean car sells faster, and a car that sits unsold for weeks tends to sell for less.
  • It removes easy bargaining chips. Buyers who cannot find fault do not open with a low offer.
  • It will not hide mechanical issues, and it should not try to. Declare what you know; a buyer who finds a problem you concealed will walk, and may come back afterwards.
  • If the car has real cosmetic damage, put it right separately. A gleaming car with a kerbed alloy still reads as a kerbed alloy.

Handing over the service history, both keys and a clean car together is what makes a buyer feel confident enough to pay the asking price.

FAQs

Frequently asked questions

How does the Ultimate Pre-Sale Valet help increase my car's resale value?
It goes beyond cleaning — restoring shine, removing light scratches and odours, and enhancing overall presentation. A well-detailed car attracts more buyers and often sells for a higher price.
How long does it take?
Typically 3 to 5 hours, depending on the size and condition of the vehicle. Larger or heavily soiled cars may take longer.
What's the difference between this and a regular valet?
The Ultimate Pre-Sale Valet adds advanced steps like machine paint correction, upholstery conditioning and ceramic-spray protection — a deeper restoration and longer-lasting finish a standard valet doesn't include.
Will you come to my home or workplace?
Yes — Ecoverde is fully mobile. We bring everything needed, including water, power and eco-friendly products, and complete the valet at your convenience across West London.
How much more will my car sell for after a pre-sale valet?
It varies far too much by car and by buyer for anyone to give you an honest figure, and be wary of anyone who does. What is consistent is that a well-presented car sells faster and attracts less haggling, and on a private sale that combination is usually worth considerably more than the valet costs.
Should I valet before taking the photographs?
Yes, always. The photographs are what decide whether anyone comes to see the car, and you only take them once. Valet first, then photograph in soft daylight against a plain background, low and from the corners rather than standing over the car.
Is it worth valeting a car I am part-exchanging?
A good clean is worth doing, a full detail usually is not. A trade buyer values against auction prices rather than kerb appeal, so the uplift is small. That said, a genuinely dirty car invites a lower opening offer, so it is not worth turning up filthy either.
What do buyers notice first?
The smell, before they have finished sitting down. After that the wheels, the glass and the touch points, meaning the steering wheel, gear selector and door handles. Greasy, shiny plastics suggest hard use whatever the mileage says, and they are straightforward to put right.
Will a valet hide problems with the car?
No, and it should not be trying to. A valet presents the car you actually have at its best. Anything mechanical should be declared, because a buyer who discovers a concealed fault will walk away, and depending on how it was described you may hear from them again afterwards.
Should I clean the engine bay before selling?
A tidy engine bay makes a strong impression precisely because buyers do not expect one. It should be sensibly cleaned rather than steam-blasted, since forcing water into modern electrics causes problems that cost far more than the sale gained. We clean bays by hand for that reason.
How soon before viewings should the valet be done?
Ideally within a few days of taking the photographs and starting the viewings. If the car sits on a driveway under trees for three weeks afterwards you will be doing much of it again, so it is worth timing the valet to the point the car actually goes on sale.
Is it worth repairing scuffs and kerbed wheels before selling?
Usually yes, especially on a private sale. Visible cosmetic damage gives a buyer both a reason to hesitate and an obvious number to negotiate with, and the discount they ask for is generally larger than the repair costs. Those are separate jobs from the valet and are best done first.

Home/Valeting Service/Monthly Valeting Plans
Monthly Valeting Plans · West London

Monthly valeting plans

Never think about washing the car again. A monthly valeting plan keeps your vehicle consistently clean, protected and presentable — with regular scheduled visits to your home or office, priority booking and a discounted per-visit rate compared to one-off valets.

Tailored monthly plans · free quote
Call 07495 400369
Set It & Forget It

A consistently spotless car

Choose how often we visit — weekly, fortnightly or monthly — and we handle the rest. Regular care keeps paintwork protected, interiors fresh and resale value high, without you ever booking a car wash again.

  • Regular scheduled visits — weekly, fortnightly or monthly
  • Priority booking and a fixed, discounted per-visit rate
  • Same trusted technician who knows your car
  • Protects paintwork, interior & resale value over time
  • Pause, change or cancel your plan anytime
Is This You?

A monthly plan is ideal if…

Regular valeting plans suit anyone who wants a permanently presentable car without the hassle.

  • You're a busy professional with no time to clean the car
  • You want your car always presentable for clients or family
  • You'd rather not spend weekends washing the car
  • You want to protect paintwork and resale value long-term
  • You run a small fleet or several household cars
What's Included

How the plans work

Every plan is tailored to your car and schedule — here's what a typical maintenance plan includes.

Every Maintenance Visit Includes

  • Exterior safe hand wash, dry & tyre dressing
  • Interior vacuum, wipe-down and glass clean
  • Regular protection top-up to keep paint beading
  • Quick, tidy and fully mobile at your address

Plan Benefits

  • Discounted per-visit rate versus one-off valets
  • Priority slots — your regular time is reserved
  • Flexible frequency — scale up before events or seasons
  • No lock-in — pause or cancel anytime
Simple & Flexible

How monthly plans work

Set your schedule once and we keep your car looking its best all year.

01

Tell Us Your Car & Schedule

Message us your vehicle, postcode and how often you'd like us to visit. We'll recommend a plan and send a clear monthly quote.

02

We Set Your Regular Slot

Your preferred day and time are reserved on a recurring basis, so you never have to rebook or chase an appointment.

03

We Come to You

Our technician arrives on schedule with everything needed and completes your maintenance valet at home or work.

04

Stay Spotless Year-Round

Your car stays consistently clean and protected. Adjust, pause or cancel your plan anytime — no lock-in.

Fully Insured & DBS-Checked Eco-Friendly Products Fully Mobile — We Come to You 5.0 from 560+ Reviews
Plans & Pricing

Choose your maintenance plan

Built for busy drivers who want the car looking sharp every day without lifting a finger. Every plan uses biodegradable, low-water products and is carried out at your home or workplace.

PlanWhat you getHow oftenPrice
Essential ShineOne Mini Valet a month: eco-friendly hand wash, wheels and tyres, glass clean, light interior vacuum and a dashboard wipe-down.MonthlyFrom £75/month
Premium CareTwo Mini Valets a month, plus a full interior vacuum and wipe-down, tyre dressing and door shuts cleaned.FortnightlyFrom £140/month
Executive Fleet CareA weekly exterior hand wash and quick interior tidy. Built for business cars and daily drivers that need to look client-ready at all times.WeeklyFrom £160/month

Yearly plans

For drivers who want deeper protection and better value, the annual plans combine regular valets with ceramic coating care.

PlanWhat you getPrice
Seasonal RefreshQuarterlyFour Full Valets a year, one each season, plus priority booking slots.From £680/year
Ceramic Protection PlanAn IGL-certified ceramic coating application, plus two Mini Valets a year to keep the coating performing at its best.From £549/year
Ultimate Annual CarePremium Care valets all year round on a fortnightly visit, a ceramic coating top-up and unlimited priority rebooking.From £1,499/year

A note on pricing. Plan prices vary with the size and condition of your vehicle, exactly as our one-off bookings do. Send us a photo of the car and we will confirm your exact monthly or annual figure before anything starts. The car valeting cost guide explains how our individual services are priced.

The Case For It

Why regular beats occasional

A car cleaned every few months and a car cleaned every month are not the same car with different schedules. The difference is what gets the chance to bond to the paint in between.

  • Contamination etches with time. Bird droppings and tree sap are acidic and start marking clear coat within days in warm weather. Removed quickly they leave nothing; left for a month they leave a permanent mark.
  • Traffic film builds in layers. Once it has been through a few wet and dry cycles it stops washing off and starts needing chemical decontamination.
  • Brake dust is corrosive when hot. On wheels it bonds into the finish and eventually pits it.
  • Interiors are easier to keep than to rescue. A stain wiped this week is nothing. The same stain in three months has cured into the fibre.

The practical result is that maintained cars need far less correction work, and hold their finish for years rather than needing machine polishing to recover it.

London Specifically

What West London does to a car

Where the car lives matters more than how far it is driven.

ConditionWhat it doesWhy a plan helps
On-street parking under treesSap, blossom and bird droppings, constantlyThe single strongest case for monthly attention. Damage here is cumulative and permanent
Heavy stop-start trafficFar more brake dust than open-road drivingWheels cleaned before the dust bonds rather than after
Construction and roadworks dustA gritty film that scratches if wiped dryRemoved safely with lubrication rather than smeared across the paint
Winter road saltAttacks arches, sills and underbodyRegular rinsing through the worst months is genuinely protective, not cosmetic
What You Get

A maintenance visit is not a full valet

It is worth being clear about the difference, because they serve different purposes.

Maintenance visitFull valet
PurposeKeep a clean car cleanRecover a car that needs it
Typical timeAround an hourTwo to three hours or more
ExteriorSafe hand wash, wheels, glass, dry, protection topped upFull decontamination, tar and iron removal, sometimes polishing
InteriorVacuum, surfaces wiped, glass, matsDeep clean, shampoo and extraction, leather treatment
FrequencyMonthly or fortnightlyOnce or twice a year, or before a sale

Most plans work best as a full valet at the start to bring the car up to standard, then maintenance visits to hold it there.

Practicalities

How the plans actually run

  • We come to you, at home or at work, so nothing needs dropping off or collecting.
  • The same technician wherever possible, so someone who knows your car and its particular problem areas is looking after it.
  • A regular slot, so it happens without you having to remember to arrange it.
  • Flexible on frequency. Monthly suits most, fortnightly suits cars parked under trees or doing high mileage, and every six weeks is enough for a garaged car.
  • Pause it when you need to. Holidays, a car off the road, a month abroad. It is a standing arrangement, not a contract to be argued out of.

Tell us where the car is kept, how it is used and how often you would like us, and we will suggest a sensible schedule rather than selling you the largest one.

FAQs

Frequently asked questions

How much does a monthly plan cost?
Plans are tailored to your car, chosen frequency and services, at a discounted per-visit rate. Tell us what you need and we'll send a clear monthly quote.
Can I change how often you visit?
Yes — you can scale your frequency up or down anytime, for example a more thorough valet before a season change or an event.
Is there a contract or lock-in?
No — plans are flexible. You can pause, change or cancel anytime with no long-term commitment.
Do you cover multiple cars or a small fleet?
Yes — we can set up a plan for several household cars or a small business fleet, with a rate to match.
How often should I have my car valeted?
Monthly suits most cars in West London. Fortnightly is more realistic if you park on-street under trees or cover high mileage, and every six weeks is usually enough for a car kept in a garage. What matters more than the interval is consistency, because the damage that costs money is cumulative.
What is the difference between a maintenance visit and a full valet?
A full valet recovers a car, and takes two to three hours or more with full decontamination inside and out. A maintenance visit keeps an already clean car clean, and takes around an hour. Most plans start with a full valet to bring the car up to standard, then maintenance visits to hold it there.
Is a monthly plan actually cheaper than booking as needed?
Per visit, yes, and the larger saving is what you avoid. A maintained car rarely needs paint correction, because contamination never gets the chance to bond and etch. Recovering neglected paint costs several times more than keeping good paint good.
Do I need to be there when you come?
No, as long as we can reach the car and there is somewhere sensible to work. Many customers leave a key or simply leave the car on the drive. If we need access to the interior and you are out, we will arrange that with you in advance.
What happens if it rains on my scheduled day?
We rearrange, usually to the next day or two. Light drizzle is workable for a maintenance wash, but heavy rain makes a proper job impossible and we would rather move it than do it badly. You are not charged for a visit we have moved.
Can I pause or cancel the plan?
Yes. Pause it for a holiday, a car off the road or a spell abroad, and pick it back up when you need it. It is a standing arrangement rather than a fixed contract, and we would rather keep customers because the work is good than because they cannot get out of it.
Will the same person clean my car each time?
Wherever possible, yes. Someone who has cleaned your car before knows where it collects dirt, which wheels take the brake dust and which trim needs care, and the result is better for it.
Does regular valeting really protect the paint?
Yes, and it is the most practical protection there is. Acidic contamination such as bird droppings and tree sap etches clear coat within days in warm weather. Removed promptly it leaves nothing behind. Left for weeks it leaves a mark that needs machine polishing to remove, if it can be removed at all.
Explore More

Other services

Valeting Service

A full deep clean inside & out.

View service

Ultimate Pre-Sale Valet

Showroom finish before you sell.

View service

Mobile Car Wash

Quick, eco-friendly exterior wash.

View service

Just bought a used car?

Our Used Car Fresh Start Valet deep cleans and steam sanitises the whole interior, then treats smoke, pet, damp and food smells at the source rather than covering them up. Fully mobile across West London, from £189.

Why valet a used car after buying it?

You don't know how the last owner used it. Seats, carpets, vents and the steering wheel hold dirt, bacteria and old smells, so a deep clean and steam sanitisation gives you a hygienic start.

How long does it take?

Usually 2 to 4 hours, depending on the size of the car and its condition.

Ready When You Are

Keep your car spotless all year

Tell us your car and schedule for a free monthly-plan quote. Fully mobile across West London, 7 days a week.

Home/Gift Vouchers
Gift Vouchers · West London

Car valeting gift vouchers

A gift for someone who loves their car, or for anyone who would rather not spend a Saturday cleaning one. Vouchers are personalised, sent by email and redeemable anywhere across our West London coverage.

Open value cards from £25
Why It Works

A gift that gets used

Most gifts sit in a drawer. A valet gets booked, turns up at their door and leaves them with a car that feels new again. It suits people who are hard to buy for, and it works just as well for a new driver as for someone who has owned the same car for a decade.

  • Nothing to post. The voucher arrives by email, so it can be arranged the night before if you have left it late.
  • Nothing for them to arrange in advance. They get in touch whenever suits and we come to them.
  • No wasted value. A voucher can be put towards a bigger service if they want something more extensive.
  • Genuinely useful. Especially for new parents, new car owners, or anyone whose car lives on the street.
Voucher Ideas

Something for every occasion

All vouchers can be personalised with a message and issued digitally. If none of these quite fit, an open value card lets them choose for themselves.

Open Value Gift Card

£25 upwards

Let them choose their own service. Ideal when you are not sure whether they want a quick refresh or a full detail.

New Car Sparkle Package

Full valet

A full valet for someone who has just picked up a new, or new to them, car. A good way to start ownership properly.

Ceramic Coating Gift Experience

Premium

A voucher for our IGL-certified ceramic coating. The one to choose for a genuine car enthusiast.

Mother's Day or Father's Day Treat

Popular

A mobile valet booked around their day and carried out at home, so they do not have to go anywhere.

Wedding Car Detail Voucher

Occasion

For the bridal car, or for the groom's pride and joy, valeted to perfection before the big day.

Christmas & New Year Voucher

Seasonal

A seasonal design that makes an easy stocking filler for anyone who loves their car.

Corporate Thank You Voucher

Bulk available

For businesses rewarding staff or thanking clients. Can be bought in bulk with your own message.

Birthday Detail Voucher

Anytime

A simple, thoughtful gift for a birthday, easy to arrange at short notice.

How It Works

Four steps, start to finish

  1. 1
    Tell us what you have in mind

    Message us with the occasion, who it is for and roughly what you would like to spend. If you are not sure, the open value card covers it.

  2. 2
    We confirm the amount and wording

    We will suggest the service that fits the budget, and you tell us the name and any personal message you would like on the voucher.

  3. 3
    We send the voucher

    It arrives by email, ready to forward or print. Corporate orders can be issued in bulk.

  4. 4
    They arrange the visit

    The recipient gets in touch whenever suits them and we come to their address anywhere in our West London coverage.

Not sure what to choose? Tell us the occasion and your budget and we will suggest the service that fits. If the recipient's car turns out to need something different, the value carries across. See the car valeting cost guide for what our individual services cost, or the maintenance plans if you would rather gift ongoing care.

Who It Suits

When a voucher lands well

After eight years of doing this across West London, a few situations come up again and again where a valet is the gift people actually remember.

  • New parents. Car seats, crumbs, spilled bottles and no time. This is the single most appreciated voucher we issue.
  • Someone who has just bought a used car. A proper first clean removes the previous owner from it, which matters more to people than they expect.
  • Anyone parking on the street. Tree sap, bird mess and traffic film build up fast in London, and a voucher is a practical answer rather than a novelty.
  • The person who is impossible to buy for. If they already own everything, they still have a car that needs cleaning.
  • Someone selling soon. A pre-sale valet often returns more than it costs, so the gift pays for itself.
  • Staff and clients. Corporate vouchers stand out because they give somebody a Saturday back.

Christmas, Father’s Day and weddings are our busiest periods for vouchers, so it is worth ordering a few days ahead at those times. Outside them we can usually turn one around the same day.

FAQs

Frequently asked questions

How much is a gift voucher?
Open value gift cards start at £25 and you can choose any amount above that. If you would rather gift a specific service, we will tell you the exact figure for that service based on the recipient's vehicle, or issue the voucher for a set amount that they can put towards it.
How long is a voucher valid for?
Twelve months from the date we issue it. If a voucher is close to expiring and the recipient has not been able to use it, get in touch and we will sort something out rather than let it go to waste.
Can I add a personal message?
Yes. Tell us the recipient's name and whatever you would like it to say, and we will put it on the voucher before sending it.
How is the voucher delivered?
By email, so it can be forwarded straight on or printed at home. That also means it can be arranged at very short notice if you have left it late.
Where can the voucher be used?
Anywhere in our West London coverage, including Brentford, Ladbroke Grove, Chiswick, Ealing, Kew, Richmond, Notting Hill and Chelsea. We are fully mobile, so we come to the recipient's home or workplace.
Can the recipient put it towards a more expensive service?
Yes. A voucher can be used as part payment against any service we offer, so they can top it up if they would like something more extensive than the voucher covers.
Can I buy vouchers for my staff or clients?
Yes. Corporate vouchers can be issued in bulk with your own message, which is a popular option for rewarding a team or thanking clients at the end of a year.
What if the recipient does not want the service on the voucher?
They can swap it for another service of the same value, or put the value towards something else. We would rather they had something they actually want.
Gift Vouchers

Give a car they will enjoy getting back into

Tell us the occasion and the budget, and we will have a personalised voucher in your inbox. Fully mobile across West London, 7 days a week.

WhatsApp Us

Whether the mould is under the seats, in the carpets or around the boot, we assess it at your home or workplace in West London. Most treatments take 2 to 4 hours.

Fully Insured & DBS-Checked Eco-Friendly Products Fully Mobile — We Come to You 5.0 from 560+ Reviews
First Things First

Find the water, or it comes back

Mould in a car is a symptom. Something is letting water in, or trapping it, and unless that is found the smell returns within weeks of any clean. So we look for the source before we treat anything.

SourceTell-tale signFix
Blocked sunroof drainsDamp headlining, water down the A-pillar, wet front carpetFour small drain tubes, one at each corner, clogged with leaf debris. Usually clearable
Perished door or window sealsDamp along the sill, water in the door cardSeal replacement, though cleaning the channel sometimes helps
Blocked pollen filter housing drainDamp passenger footwell, musty air from the ventsClearing the drain and replacing the cabin filter
Boot seal or light cluster sealsWater in the spare wheel wellReseating or replacing the seal
Heater matrix leakSweet smell, greasy film on the inside of the windscreen, wet passenger sideA garage job. That is coolant, not rainwater, and we will tell you
Wet items left in the carLocalised damp under mats or in the bootThe most common of all. Gym kit, umbrellas, dog towels
Why It Matters

Damp is a health issue, not just a smell

A car cabin is a small, sealed, warm space. Mould growing in carpet underlay or in the air conditioning is circulated straight into the air you breathe every time the fan comes on.

  • Spores blown from the vents can aggravate asthma and allergies, and are a common cause of headaches on longer drives.
  • The cabin filter stops being a filter once it is saturated, and starts distributing what is growing in it.
  • Damp underlay stays wet long after the carpet above it feels dry, which is why surface drying rarely solves anything.
  • It is worse for children, who sit lower in the car and closer to rear footwell vents.
Masking vs Removing

Why air fresheners make it worse

Almost everyone tries the cheap options first, and they are worth understanding before you spend more on them.

  • Air fresheners and hanging trees add a scent on top. The mould is still growing, and the combination is usually more unpleasant than the original smell.
  • Odour bombs and foggers sanitise the air and the surfaces they reach. They do not reach into wet underlay, which is where the growth actually is.
  • Carpet shampoo without extraction adds more water to a car that already has too much, and frequently makes the problem worse.
  • Leaving windows open helps a damp car and does nothing for a leaking one.

Removal means taking the moisture out, killing the growth in the material rather than on it, and stopping the water getting back in.

The Process

Our 6-stage mould and damp treatment

  1. 1
    Locate the source

    A careful check of drains, seals, footwells and carpets. There is no point cleaning a car that is still letting water in.

  2. 2
    Dry it out thoroughly

    Including under the carpet where necessary. Underlay holds water long after the surface feels dry.

  3. 3
    Remove the growth

    Hot steam kills mould in the fibres rather than wiping it off the surface, and it does so without soaking the car further.

  4. 4
    Extract, do not just wash

    Wet extraction pulls the contamination and the moisture back out instead of pushing both deeper.

  5. 5
    Treat the ventilation system

    A new cabin filter and an antibacterial treatment through the evaporator, because a clean carpet and a mouldy air conditioning system still smells.

  6. 6
    Confirm it is dry before we leave

    And tell you plainly what needs a garage rather than a valeter.

FAQs

Frequently asked questions

Can you actually remove mould, or just cover the smell?
We remove it at the source — professional anti-fungal solutions and high-temperature steam kill the spores, and enzyme neutralisers break down odour molecules rather than masking them with fragrance.
What causes mould in a car?
Trapped moisture — a small leak, wet footwells, a damp boot or condensation. We find and flag the source so the mould doesn't simply come back after cleaning.
What is ozone treatment?
An ozone generator fills the cabin and air-con system with ozone gas, which penetrates fabrics and vents to eliminate stubborn, deeply embedded odours that surface cleaning can't reach.
Is it safe and eco-friendly?
Yes — we use eco-friendly, pH-balanced products and steam. After an ozone treatment the car is fully aired out before you drive, so it's safe to use.
How long does it take?
Most mould and odour treatments take 2–4 hours depending on how widespread it is; heavily affected cars or ozone treatments may need a little longer.
Why does my car smell musty even after I clean it?
Because the water is still getting in, or has never fully come out. Carpet underlay holds moisture long after the surface feels dry, and mould growing underneath keeps producing the smell. Cleaning the surface treats the symptom. Until the drain, seal or wet item causing it is dealt with, the smell returns within weeks.
What causes damp in a car?
Most often blocked sunroof drains, which are four small tubes running down the pillars and clog with leaf debris. After that, perished door and window seals, a blocked drain in the pollen filter housing, boot or light cluster seals, and simply leaving wet things in the car. A sweet smell with a greasy film on the inside of the windscreen is different: that is a leaking heater matrix and needs a garage.
Is mould in a car actually dangerous?
It is worth taking seriously. A cabin is small, warm and sealed, and spores growing in the carpet or the air conditioning get circulated straight into the air you breathe whenever the fan runs. It commonly aggravates asthma and allergies and causes headaches on longer journeys, and it affects children more because they sit lower and closer to the rear vents.
Do odour bombs or foggers work?
They sanitise the air and the surfaces they can reach, which helps with a stale car. They do not reach into wet underlay, and that is where the growth causing the smell usually lives. If the smell returns a fortnight after a fogger, that is the reason.
Can you remove the smell without finding the leak?
We can improve it substantially, and it will come back. We would rather tell you that at the outset than take payment for a result that will not last. Where we can find and clear the source, such as a blocked sunroof drain, we will. Where it needs a garage, such as a heater matrix or a failed seal, we will tell you what to ask for.
How long does mould and damp removal take?
Typically half a day, and sometimes longer where carpets need lifting and drying properly. It is not a job that can be rushed, because the drying stage decides whether the result lasts. We would rather book the time than come back twice.
Why does my air conditioning smell but the carpets are dry?
That is a different problem with a different fix. Moisture condenses on the evaporator behind the dashboard and never fully dries, so bacteria and mould grow there and get blown into the cabin. It is treated with an antibacterial treatment through the system and a new cabin filter, not by cleaning the interior.
Will the carpets need replacing?
Rarely. Most damp and mould we see comes out with proper drying, steam and wet extraction. Replacement only becomes the honest answer where a car has stood wet for a long time and the underlay has broken down, or where contamination has soaked into the sound deadening. We will say so if we find it rather than charging you for a clean that cannot work.
